roles.name: Visionary Lead
roles.aim: Build the team that builds Amora. Hold the frequency of what Amora is becoming. Bring the right people into the project.
roles.domain: Strategy and direction. Vision alignment across documents, entities, website, and team. Relationship building with investors, advisors, and aligned leaders. Culture and team coherence. Final word on questions that affect the whole org and cannot be decided inside a single circle.
accountabilities: Stewards the Purpose Statement, the Amora vision, and how that vision shows up in every document, agreement, and entity
Represents Amora in its most important relationships: investors, collaborators, potential residents, future neighbors
Hosts experiences on the land: tours, potlucks, connection gatherings
Participates in the Leadership Circle as a circle member
Curates the Wisdom Council, the Advisory Board, and specialist advisor relationships
Holds final alignment authority on Amora's seven priorities
roles.whyItMatters: When Amora's documents, entities, and governance are strong enough that the vision lives in the system and not just in one person, this role shifts fully into community building and relationship weaving. The health of this role is a measure of the health of the whole system.

roles.name: Development Lead
roles.aim: Hold the full physical realization of Amora from master plan through built-out village. Lead the team and partners that turn drawings into homes, community buildings, water systems, roads, and regenerative landscapes.
roles.domain: Master planning. Architecture and building design. Permitting and regulatory compliance. Construction oversight. Infrastructure (water, power, roads, waste, internet). Regenerative agriculture and permaculture system design. Landscape and land stewardship. Contractor management. Materials sourcing at scale.
accountabilities: Represents the physical development domain in the Leadership Circle
Holds the master plan and drives it to decisions and completion
Leads and grows the Architecture Circle, the Regenerative Agriculture and Permaculture Circle, and the Development Circle roles
Manages the primary development partnerships and any secondary bids
Owns permitting, construction timelines, and the phased build-out budget in coordination with the Finance Lead
Integrates architecture, permaculture, and land stewardship into one coherent physical plan
Reports to the Leadership Circle on development status, blockers, and decisions that need cross-circle consent
roles.whyItMatters: Amora lives or dies on whether the physical place gets built well. Without this role, the vision stays a vision. With it, the team has a partner at the top of the house who can answer 'when will this be built and by whom' with confidence.

roles.name: Finance Lead
roles.aim: Steward the financial health of Amora across all entities. Build the business development work that funds the vision. Hold the CFO function for Amora as it grows.
roles.domain: Financial operations across entities. Cash flow, budgeting, investor reporting. Investor relations and capital strategy. Revenue model development. Legal and governance structuring in coordination with counsel. Standard operating procedures for the team.
accountabilities: Holds the financial model and all its projections
Manages investor relationships and communications
Structures and negotiates financing terms
Coordinates tax and compliance across jurisdictions
Builds the infrastructure of how the team works: documents, SOPs, workflows
Represents Amora to external financial and legal stakeholders
Operations leader of the Finance & Business Circle
roles.whyItMatters: This role is the bridge between the vision and the capital that realizes it. It translates heart language into the language investors and regulators understand, and holds the structures that let the money flow in ways that honor what Amora is trying to be.

roles.name: Community Lead
roles.aim: Hold the human side of Amora. Coordinate across all the circles so the team functions as a team, not as five people working in parallel. Make sure community onboarding, events, culture, membership, and sales actually happen.
roles.domain: Cross-circle coordination. Community Circle leadership. Outreach & Growth Circle oversight. Event curation and hosting. Rites of passage and culture practices. Conflict resolution. Team health and rhythms. Governance implementation.
accountabilities: Represents the community and coordination domain in the Leadership Circle
Leads the Community Circle and holds cross-circle coordination across all circles
Makes sure each functional circle meets, produces outcomes, and surfaces tensions
Runs or oversees community onboarding, member journeys, events, and culture work
Oversees the Outreach & Growth Circle so marketing, sales, and membership work as one journey
Implements and maintains the sociocratic structure in practice
roles.whyItMatters: A village is a living human system. Without someone whose whole job is tending the people and the coordination between them, a community-in-formation either burns out its founders or fractures as it grows. This role is what lets Amora scale from five people to fifty without losing its soul.

roles.name: Operations Steward
roles.aim: Make the team's work together run without friction. Hold the rhythms, the rituals, the follow-through, and the structure that lets everyone else do their work.
roles.domain: Weekly and monthly meeting rhythms (Monday and Friday syncs, agenda, notes, follow-ups). Team coordination across all circles. Document organization. Project tracking. Internal SOPs. Scheduling.
accountabilities: Owns the meeting rhythm: agenda prep, notes, to-do list updates, follow-through
Maintains the shared team folder so documents are findable
Tracks cross-circle projects so nothing falls through
Supports document creation: memos, proposals, slide decks
Keeps the governance work moving between meetings
Reports on team health and flow back into the General Circle
roles.whyItMatters: This is the role that turns talented people with overlapping work into one coherent team. Without it, everyone does their best but the team itself does not cohere. With it, each person gets to spend their time on the work that only they can do.

roles.name: Chief of Staff / Executive Assistant
roles.aim: Multiply the leadership team's capacity. Hold the follow-through, communications triage, and administration so leaders spend their time on the work only they can do.
roles.domain: Founder and leadership support. Communications triage. Scheduling and calendar protection. Hiring administration and structured screening support. Follow-up and relationship continuity. AI-enabled executive support.
accountabilities: Triages inbound communications so nothing urgent is missed and nothing minor interrupts deep work
Protects leadership calendars and prepares the context each meeting needs
Runs first screening for open seats against explicit criteria
Keeps a clear record of commitments and follow-ups so scarcity never creates informal promises
Carries relationship continuity: the thank-you, the follow-up note, the next step
Works hand in hand with the team's living-memory systems as they come online
roles.whyItMatters: Every hour of administration this role absorbs is an hour of vision, relationship, and decision-making returned to the people the village most needs doing that work. Some of this role's scope may shift to Sera, the team's living-memory system, over time.

roles.name: Website & Backend/AI
roles.aim: Build and steward Amora's digital nervous system: the website people meet first, and Sera, the living memory where roles, decisions, and institutional knowledge stay current.
roles.domain: The Amora website. Sera, the backend and AI living-memory system. Integration between the roles/circles platform, Sera, and the website so the team can update roles, write job descriptions, and open applications live.
accountabilities: Builds and maintains the public website
Develops Sera as the home of Amora's institutional data, decisions, and roles
Integrates the roles/circles platform with Sera and the website
Keeps the organization's structure editable by the team, not routed through one person
Supports the rest of the team with the digital tools their circles need
roles.whyItMatters: When the organization's structure lives in a system instead of one person's head, roles, job posts, and applications update in real time, and the team stops routing every small change through a single bottleneck.

roles.name: Marketing Steward
roles.aim: Open the Amora flower so the right bees find it. Attract aligned future neighbors, investors, and collaborators through clear, honest, on-brand communications.
roles.domain: All outward-facing marketing and communications. Website copy, CRM, email flows, newsletter, webinars. Messaging strategy. Lot sales funnel. Marketing team coordination.
accountabilities: Writes and maintains the messaging Amora puts into the world
Builds and runs the email nurture sequences in the CRM
Manages the marketing team and the budget that supports it
Promotes events: village weaving, land tours, potlucks, family days, webinars
Creates and runs the funnel that takes someone from 'heard of Amora' to 'applying to be a neighbor'
Reports monthly on marketing KPIs
roles.whyItMatters: Marketing done wrong pulls in the wrong people. This role is the filter that ensures the people arriving at the door are already resonant, so the cultural fit is there before they even show up. It also writes Amora into the broader story of what a new kind of village can be.

roles.name: Sales Lead
roles.aim: Build the sales team and walk aligned people from first interest to real commitment: home sales, lot sales, and the relationships that fund the village.
roles.domain: The full sales function: qualification, scheduling, CRM, follow-up, pricing conversations, documents, objections, next steps, closing, and transaction coordination. Building and leading the sales team as it grows.
accountabilities: Builds out the sales team, a confirmed gap the village is actively hiring for
Owns follow-up, diligence, economics, negotiation, and closing so momentum never depends on one person's calendar
Runs the handoff from marketing's first contact into a real human relationship
Coordinates pricing, documents, and terms with the Finance Lead
Keeps the journey honest: the goal is the right neighbors, not the fastest close
roles.whyItMatters: The founder creates trust and resonance; a competent sales team owns everything after that. This circle connects with people and guides their whole journey into the village. Sales is the bridge between resonance and commitment.

roles.name: Social Media Steward
roles.holderNote: One person holds this today; a second may join as the work grows.
roles.aim: Carry Amora's story into the feeds where future neighbors, collaborators, and investors first hear of it.
roles.domain: Social channels, short-form content, and the day-to-day storytelling rhythm, in coordination with the Marketing Steward and media team.
accountabilities: Creates and publishes the ongoing social storytelling of Amora
Coordinates with photographers, videographers, and the marketing funnel
Turns land days, events, and milestones into shareable moments
Keeps the tone honest and on-brand: resonance over reach
roles.whyItMatters: Most people's first glimpse of Amora is a thirty-second story. This role decides whether that glimpse carries the real thing.

roles.name: Membership and Onboarding Steward
roles.aim: Hold the journey a person walks from curious visitor to committed member of the Amora Family. Make sure every step is coherent, welcoming, and honest.
roles.domain: The Love Letter (membership agreement). The waitlist for residents. The rites of passage: Co-Creator, Resident. Background checks. Application flows. The handoff from first contact into deep relationship, inside the same circle that made the first contact.
accountabilities: Maintains the Love Letter and the membership process
Runs the waitlist and the right-of-refusal process for lots
Coordinates the rites of passage across Village Steward, Resident, and Prosperity journeys
Manages background checks and the vetting process
Acts as the point of contact for someone in the middle of their journey
roles.whyItMatters: Amora's central innovation is the filtering journey itself. Most intentional communities fail because they let the wrong people in too fast. This role is the guardian of cultural coherence at the point of entry. It lives inside the Outreach & Growth Circle so the same circle that connects with people also guides their whole journey in.

roles.name: Community Engagement Steward
roles.aim: Make the in-person experience of Amora one people want to tell their friends about. Welcome guests. Run the events that are the entry point for most people.
roles.domain: Weekly potluck and seasonal retreats. Event management, communication, preparation, setup, breakdown, transportation. Hospitality and guest coordination on the land. Team communications about who is visiting, when, and where they stay.
accountabilities: Runs the weekly potluck end to end
Coordinates who is on the land at any given time and what they need
Represents Amora to guests face to face
Manages the communications Amora sends and receives day to day
Coordinates with whoever is hosting and cleaning spaces for incoming guests
roles.whyItMatters: Most people's first taste of Amora is a potluck, a land tour, or a visit. This role is the one that decides whether their first taste is 'these people are the real thing.' It is frontline culture work and it matters more than the org chart makes it look.

roles.name: Campground and Events Steward
roles.aim: Turn the Amora land into a place people can stay and experience, before they become neighbors. Create abundance from the land by welcoming aligned guests.
roles.domain: Campground design, infrastructure (tents, places to stay), and online booking. Event hosting on the land open to visitors: village weaving immersions, retreats, world-schooling families. Online presence for the stay experience.
accountabilities: Designs the Amora stay experience from first contact to departure
Orders and maintains the infrastructure: tents, common areas, stay amenities
Writes the copy and imagery that attracts the right visitors
Runs the booking system
Co-creates village weaving events and other immersions
Connects with the education work so world-schooling families have a pathway in
roles.whyItMatters: Staying on the land is one of the rites of passage. Without a campground steward, that rite has no container. This role is what makes the onboarding journey real.

roles.name: Governance, People & Team Coherence
roles.aim: Keep the human systems healthy: sociocracy in practice, team coherence, and a trusted path for tensions and conflict.
roles.domain: Sociocracy implementation support. Meeting and decision hygiene. Conduct and grievance pathways. Team health practices. A sub-circle of the Community Circle.
accountabilities: Maintains the governance agreements and keeps them current as the team evolves
Supports circles in running clean consent-based decisions
Holds the conflict and grievance pathway: serious grievances travel to the Leadership Circle or an independent facilitator, never through one person alone
Tends team health: rhythms, load, and the early signs of burnout
roles.whyItMatters: A sub-circle under the Community Lead for now, with a deliberately independent escalation path: the person coordinating performance should never be the only door for conduct concerns. As the team grows, this may become its own seat.

roles.name: Project Manager
roles.aim: Manage daily land operations and small projects. Turn plans into finished work on the ground.
roles.domain: Day-to-day land operations. Coordination of caretakers, contractors, repairs, roads, materials, and site logistics. Small-project delivery from scope to done.
accountabilities: Coordinates caretakers and contractors working on the land
Manages repairs, roads, materials runs, and site logistics
Carries small projects from scope through completion
Keeps the team informed on what is happening on the ground and what it needs
Works with the Development Lead on sequencing and budget
roles.whyItMatters: Vision without execution on the ground is a drawing. This role is the daily heartbeat of the physical project, the reason things actually get finished.

roles.name: Land Steward
roles.aim: Steward the land and its structures, with the Rancho renovation as the first big charge. Coordinate contractors, source materials, and bring the renovation to completion.
roles.domain: The Rancho renovation project and caretakers house improvements. Contractor management. Budget tracking against approved phases. Materials sourcing including kitchen equipment. Kitchen design execution. Composting toilet installation. Bodega expansion. Water system coordination.
accountabilities: Holds the renovation timeline and phase plan
Gets quotes from contractors by phase and brings them to the team for budget approval
Coordinates with the Finance team on contract creation and legal review
Sources materials: kitchen equipment, solar generators, signage, and more
Works with interior design specialist advisors if engaged
Reports on progress weekly
roles.whyItMatters: The Rancho is the physical container for the core team, volunteers, guests, and eventually the school. Until it is done, most other priorities are slowed. This role is the one that unblocks the ground game of Amora.

roles.name: Land Liaison
roles.aim: Care for the land of Amora. Hold the relationships with the people who live on it, work on it, and visit it.
roles.domain: Land management in coordination with caretakers and permaculture people. Building, planting, maintenance, guest coordination from the land side. Mapping and documentation of what is planted and where. Land tours. Day-to-day scope still taking shape.
accountabilities: Primary point of contact for caretakers and contractors working on the land
Oversees plantings, tree health, permaculture systems
Keeps the map of what is where up to date: trees, plantings, structures
Maintains common spaces and infrastructure
Gives relaxed, connected land tours to visitors
Coordinates with whoever is staying on the land
roles.whyItMatters: The land is the first resident. Every decision the team makes either deepens the relationship with the land or takes from it. This role is the one that keeps the team honest about that, and gets to spend the most time in the thing Amora is actually about.

roles.name: Architecture Circle Lead
roles.aim: Lead the design and architectural development of Amora in a regenerative, place-responsive way. Activate the Architecture Circle and get to decisions on building style and master plan.
roles.domain: Architectural design. Building style decisions. Master planning in coordination with Architecture Circle members and infrastructure advisors. Coordination with regenerative architects and the broader regenerative architecture network. Permitting and regulatory compliance on structures.
accountabilities: Activates and runs the Architecture Circle with clear agreements
Holds the master plan process with circle members and specialist advisors
Coordinates architectural decisions across the team
Manages relationships with external architects
Brings proposals to the General Circle when decisions cross circles
roles.whyItMatters: The physical form of Amora will either reinforce the values or contradict them. Hexagonal community structures, regenerative building materials, and landscape-responsive placement are not aesthetic choices, they shape how people live together. This role ensures the bones of the place match the soul.

roles.name: Regenerative Agriculture and Permaculture Circle Lead
roles.aim: Design and implement the food, medicine, and ecosystem systems that make Amora regenerative. Activate the circle with permaculture practitioners and land stewards.
roles.domain: Regenerative agriculture system design. Permaculture planning and implementation. Food and medicine systems: gardens, orchards, medicinal plantings, apothecary. Integration with on-land work. Coordination with the Architecture Circle on siting and water.
accountabilities: Activates and runs the Regenerative Ag and Permaculture Circle
Designs the regenerative systems map for Amora: food, water, soil, biodiversity
Coordinates with the Project Manager and Land Steward on day-to-day implementation
Holds the relationships with permaculture consultants and practitioners
Integrates food and medicine systems with the campground, school, and retreat offerings
Brings the regenerative systems plan to the General Circle for consent
roles.whyItMatters: Amora calls itself regenerative. Until the land is producing food, medicine, and ecosystem health, that word is aspirational. This circle is what makes the word real.

roles.name: Business Development Steward
roles.holderNote: Held by Ky alongside the Finance Lead seat. The village is seeking a full-time steward for this role.
roles.aim: Develop the revenue-generating projects that fund Amora's long-term vision. Build the retreat center, the longevity center, and the village business ecosystem.
roles.domain: Strategic partnerships for business development. Retreat center design and launch. Longevity center design and launch. Amora Business Incubation Program for village businesses birthed from the community. Investor relations in coordination with the Finance Lead.
accountabilities: Scopes and develops the retreat and longevity centers
Builds the strategic partnerships that bring aligned operators to the village
Designs the business incubation program that supports village businesses
Co-develops and refines business plans with the Prosperity Circle as it forms
Supports the Prosperity Space as it populates
roles.whyItMatters: A very high priority right now. Without this role, Amora risks becoming just a place people live instead of a place where regenerative livelihoods take root. A future finance hire may free this seat to focus fully on business development and investor relations, bringing in the money that funds the vision.

roles.name: Entity and Land Trust Steward
roles.aim: Build and steward the legal container that allows Amora to hold the land, the funding, and the governance in alignment with its values.
roles.domain: Entity structure work: Church, SRL, SA, and DAO considerations. The land trust pathway. Legal agreements with investors and members. Coordination with legal and governance specialist advisors. Memos to counsel on funding pathways. Membership agreements. Permitting and construction legal stays with the Development Circle.
accountabilities: Holds the entity structure design and its current state
Prepares memos to external counsel on behalf of the team
Coordinates with specialist advisors on legal structuring, governance design, and DAO implementation
Manages membership agreements with specialist advisor input
Works with the Community Circle on how the legal container serves the onboarding journey
Reports to the General Circle on entity status and any blockers
roles.whyItMatters: The Church, the SRL, the land trust, the DAO all shape what kinds of decisions can be made and by whom. This domain is where the vision becomes legally real. Getting it wrong constrains every future choice. Getting it right unlocks the funding, the residency process, and the governance model.

roles.name: Wisdom Council
roles.aim: Provide wisdom on questions that touch culture, belonging, ceremony, and the long view.
roles.domain: Rites of passage. Guidance on culture, belonging, ceremony. Not decision-making authority over operations.
accountabilities: Meets monthly to advise the Leadership Circle and the Visionary Lead
Holds wisdom on community and indigenous practices
Advises on culture, belonging, and ceremony
Helps Amora stay connected to what communities have learned over generations
roles.whyItMatters: Amora is being built inside a culture that has forgotten most of what it knows about community. Elders hold what the culture forgot. This council is how Amora stays connected to that memory instead of trying to invent community from scratch.

roles.name: Advisory Board
roles.aim: Provide strategic counsel on development decisions and share patterns from other regenerative projects.
roles.domain: Strategic counsel on development. Pattern recognition from other regenerative projects. Connections and introductions. Not decision-making authority over operations.
accountabilities: Advises on major development and community design decisions
Brings pattern recognition from comparable projects
Provides introductions to aligned capital, talent, and partners
Helps Amora avoid pitfalls that have challenged similar projects
roles.whyItMatters: Amora is not the first regenerative project and it will not be the last. The Advisory Board is how Amora stands on the shoulders of what has already been learned instead of reinventing it.

roles.name: Board of Directors
roles.aim: Provide governance oversight on the legal entities.
roles.domain: Fiduciary oversight of the legal entities. Formal governance. Not day-to-day operational decision-making.
accountabilities: Holds fiduciary responsibility for the legal entities
Provides formal governance oversight on key decisions
Ensures investor and stakeholder interests are properly represented
Works alongside the Wisdom Council and Advisory Board
roles.whyItMatters: This is the container that holds the legal and fiduciary responsibility so the circle structure can stay focused on creating.

circles.name: General Coordinating Circle
circles.subtitle: Where the circles meet
circles.description: The coordinating heart of the team: the four leads and circle representatives, meeting in one rhythm so information flows both ways and decisions land where they belong.
circles.domain: Strategic coordination, alignment, policy, budget stewardship, team coherence, decision-making, conflict resolution, inter-circle collaboration
circles.members: Visionary Lead, Development Lead, Finance Lead, Community Lead, and circle leads

circles.name: Outreach & Growth Circle
circles.subtitle: One journey, one circle
circles.description: Connects with people and guides their whole journey into the village, from the first story they hear, through a real conversation, to membership and a home. Marketing, sales, social media, and onboarding work as one flow, not four departments.
circles.domain: Marketing and communications, sales and the sales team, social media, membership and onboarding
circles.members: Marketing Steward, Sales Lead, Social Media Steward, Membership & Onboarding Steward

circles.name: Community Circle
circles.subtitle: The human experience
circles.description: Tends the lived experience of Amora: events, hospitality, the campground and stays, and the governance and team-health practices that keep the human systems honest.
circles.domain: Events and engagement, hospitality and stays, culture practices, governance, people and team coherence
circles.members: Community Engagement Steward, Campground & Events Steward, Governance/People sub-circle

circles.name: Development Circle
circles.subtitle: From drawings to homes
circles.description: Holds the physical realization of the village: master planning, architecture, permitting, construction, infrastructure, land operations, and the regenerative systems that make the place alive.
circles.domain: Architecture, permitting, construction, infrastructure, land operations, regenerative agriculture and permaculture
circles.members: Development Lead, Project Manager, Land Steward, Land Liaison, Architecture Circle, Regen Ag & Permaculture Circle

circles.name: Finance & Business Circle
circles.subtitle: Fuel for the vision
circles.description: Stewards the money and builds the engines that generate it: financial operations, capital strategy, the legal container, and the business development that funds the long-term vision.
circles.domain: Financial operations, investor relations, entity and legal structure, business development, retreat and longevity centers, business incubation
circles.members: Finance Lead, Business Development Steward, Entity & Land Trust Steward

circles.name: Permaculture Council
circles.subtitle: Land Stewardship & Food Systems
circles.description: Cares for the land through regenerative agriculture, landscaping, and ecological restoration.
circles.domain: Food systems, regenerative agriculture, landscaping, land stewardship
circles.members: Residents involved in farming, gardening, and land management

circles.name: Education Council
circles.subtitle: Learning & Development
circles.description: Supports children's education, adult learning, and knowledge sharing across the community.
circles.domain: Children's education, adult learning, knowledge sharing

circles.name: Culture & Arts Council
circles.subtitle: Creative Expression
circles.description: Cultivates artistic expression, musical events, and cultural programming for the community.
circles.domain: Musical events, artistic expression, cultural programming
circles.members: Artists, musicians, event organizers, cultural enthusiasts

circles.name: Health & Healing Council
circles.subtitle: Wellness & Care
circles.description: Coordinates wellness services, healing modalities, and community health initiatives.
circles.domain: Wellness services, healing modalities, community health
circles.members: Health practitioners, wellness facilitators, fitness leaders

circles.name: Building & Village Council
circles.subtitle: Infrastructure & Maintenance
circles.description: Oversees construction, maintenance, infrastructure development, and architectural decisions.
circles.members: Construction-savvy residents, architects, designers, maintenance coordinators

circles.name: Business & Finance Council
circles.subtitle: Economic Sustainability
circles.description: Governs community financial decisions, business enterprises, and economic sustainability.
circles.domain: Community financial governance, enterprises, financial sustainability, local economy
circles.members: Entrepreneurs, business operators, financial managers, residents with financial expertise

circles.name: Community Life Council
circles.subtitle: Social Connection
circles.description: Coordinates social events, conflict resolution, and community celebrations.
circles.members: Social coordinators, facilitators, community builders, local representation

circles.name: Intergenerational Wisdom Council
circles.subtitle: Wisdom & Rights of Nature
circles.description: Bridges generations through elder care, children's advocacy, indigenous practices, and rights of nature.
circles.domain: Elder care, children's advocacy, indigenous practices, rights of nature, rites of passage
circles.members: Elders, parents, indigenous wisdom keepers, earth-centered practitioners

team.name: Jessica Filkins
team.bio: Visionary founder creating regenerative community infrastructure and leading Amora's evolution toward a multigenerational, family-centered village.

team.name: Kyleen Keenan
team.bio: Stewards financial strategy, investor relations, and the business development that funds the vision, holding the CFO function as Amora grows.
